prize_parts.citation: for discoveries establishing the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its bioactive form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots place B010 first, but I do not treat that agreement as the argument. The scientific case is that the work follows one coherent chain: proglucagon-derived peptides, the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, human physiology of the incretin effect and its role in appetite, receptor biology, and long-acting agonists. Large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disease have confirmed the clinical result, so the interpretation is stable. A basic-science trio of Holst, Drucker and Mojsov fits the prize's emphasis on discovery with benefit to humankind, and it is a single achievement that is easy to cite.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The credited list has four names, Habener is not credited at all, and priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for the bioactive peptide is disputed. Leaving out Knudsen means the prize honours the physiological discovery and not the drug that delivered the benefit, and some will see that as rewarding the less decisive step. Because B010 is so uniformly favoured, there is also a risk that we settle the allocation too quickly. If the committee cannot defend the three names on documented priority, the configuration fails even though the science is clearly worthy.

responses.point: Sandberg backs the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio but flags that Mojsov's priority against Habener's group is disputed and that he relies on recall, not verification.
responses.response: I agree that this is the central open question and I cannot settle it from the supplied evidence either. My view is that Mojsov's identification of the bioactive truncated peptide and early synthesis is separable from the proglucagon sequencing work, which is why I would keep her in the trio. But that depends on a documentary check of the original publications and their dates. I would not defend the configuration if that check showed her contribution to be derivative.

responses.point: Linnarsson sees the discovery-to-therapy arc as unusually complete and notes that Knudsen's industrial development was decisive for the drugs but must be traded off against a three-person limit.
responses.response: I take the point that the arc includes the drugs, and the citation should say so. But I would qualify the claim that Knudsen's role must win a seat. Her medicinal chemistry made long-acting GLP-1 agonists possible, yet the biological principle that justified them was established by the physiologists. I would keep her as the first reserve if the attribution review weakens any of the three, rather than displace a discoverer now.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranked CAR-T second with only June and Sadelain, arguing that Rosenberg's decisive contribution lies in adoptive cell therapy broadly, and ranked TNF blockade third.
responses.response: I mostly agree that Rosenberg's claim to CAR-T is less direct. I ranked the three-name version on my own ballot but now think the two-person version is more defensible, so B006 remains my first alternative with June and Sadelain. I am less convinced that B041 can compete with B010 in the same year: TNF blockade is mature and clean, but its translational story is closer to antibody therapy than to a new biological axis. That is a difference of weighting and not a dismissal.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked the unfolded protein response third as a clean two-person discovery of organelle-to-nucleus signalling with textbook maturity, and also placed CAR-T second.
responses.response: I agree that B020 is the tidiest attribution on the list, and its scientific originality is not in doubt. My reservation is that its direct relevance to medicine is mostly through disease associations, not an established intervention, which separates it from B010 on the clinical dimension. I would hold it for a later year or a two-part prize and not put it ahead of the incretin work now.

responses.point: El-Manira regards optogenetics as having opened circuit questions that were previously intractable but warns of priority disputes and that the Prize has historically favoured discoveries over techniques.
responses.response: I share both concerns. I keep B008 as my second alternative because its influence across neuroscience is exceptional, but I would not pair it with B010 in a two-part prize unless the three-name allocation (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) can be defended against Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. A single, clearly allocated achievement is stronger than a divided prize carrying an unresolved dispute.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying the bioactive GLP-1 peptide is distinct enough from the Habener group's work to justify her over an uncredited or alternative candidate.
Whether Knudsen should replace one of the academic trio, or be added, if the committee prefers to credit the drug development.
Whether a second part (CAR-T or optogenetics) would strengthen or dilute a prize that already has a well-defined single achievement.
Durability of weight-loss effects and long-term safety signals for obesity indications.
statement.conflict_note: I have co-authored with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy); this is a collaboration between colleagues, not a connection to any shortlisted candidate. My postdoctoral work with Paul Greengard also has no apparent link to any shortlisted candidate. No specific conflict with the shortlisted candidates is apparent from the provided profile.
